plan.why: Expiry, showing it and reporting on it are three outcomes customers and support see separately, so this plan has stories.
assumptions: A quote's lifetime is 24 hours for every customer, as the spec says.
Expiry is checked only when a quote is booked, so nothing runs in the background.
An expired quote is kept, so support can still look it up.
plan.order: S1, then S2 and S3 in parallel

items.title: Quotes expire after 24 hours
items.outcome: Booking a quote more than 24 hours old is refused, with a link to a new quote.
criteria: Booking a quote less than 24 hours old works as it does today.
Booking a quote more than 24 hours old returns an expired error and books nothing.
The expired error links to a new quote for the same trip.
The PWA and the MCP server both get the expired error.

items.title: Customers see when a quote expires
items.outcome: Every quote a customer sees shows the time it expires.
criteria: A new quote in the PWA shows its expiry time in the customer's time zone.
A quote from the MCP server includes its expiry time.
A quote shown after it expired says it has expired and offers a new quote.

items.title: Expired quotes in the monthly report
items.outcome: The monthly report lists expired quotes, marked as expired.
criteria: An expired quote appears in the report for the month it was issued.
The report marks each expired quote as expired.
The report's totals count booked quotes only.
